name: TeamStarWolf - The Year 2011 in Intrusions
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK Enterprise techniques that the verified 2011 record supports: the techniques ATT&CK lists for the objects it ties to 2011, campaign C0002 Night Dragon (published by McAfee on 10 February, last seen February 2011), S0038 Duqu (first recorded attack April 2011, disclosed in October) and G0006 APT1 (only the eight techniques the record opened names, from Mandiant's 2013 report that dates APT1 activity from January 2011), and behavior described by Comodo's incident report, VASCO's filing on DigiNotar, Google's and Microsoft's notices on the fraudulent certificates, US-CERT's Gmail phishing alert and Google's account of that campaign, Adobe's advisory and NVD's records for the flaws exploited at release, CrySyS Lab's and Symantec's Duqu reports, Apache's Range-header advisory, Microsoft's Morto entry, Valve's Steam message and the FBI's releases on the Sony Pictures intrusion, the PayPal attacks, Coreflood, DNSChanger and the 2011 to 2013 financial-sector DDoS, with the Stratfor card charges graded Reported. No 2011 source prints an ATT&CK id. The three ATT&CK for ICS techniques listed for Duqu are not in this layer. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/CHRONICLE_2011.md. Scores: 100 an ATT&CK object prints the id, 70 the source describes the behavior and the study assigns the id, 50 only a Reported source supports the behavior, 40 the mapping is Inferred.
